lean.statement: For every finite type iota, probability measure mu on EuclideanSpace real iota, nonzero real eta, and centers y y', RelativeFisher.information mu (fun x => 1) (fun t => -(norm (t-y))^2/(2*eta) - log (integral z, exp (-(norm (z-y))^2/(2*eta)) dmu) - (-(norm (t-y'))^2/(2*eta)) + log (integral z, exp (-(norm (z-y'))^2/(2*eta)) dmu) = eta^{-1}^2 * (norm (y-y'))^2.
approved_definition_context: RelativeFisher.information base q r is the integral against base of q(x) times the squared norm of the spatial gradient of r at x.
A probability-measure instance states that the total mass of the measure is one.
EuclideanSpace real iota is the finite-dimensional real Euclidean state space indexed by a finite type.
The two displayed integrals and their real logarithms are constants with respect to the spatial variable t.
Real inverse and powers use Lean's ordinary total real-number operations; the explicit hypothesis eta nonzero selects the intended division domain.
